newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Cargo boosts E Europe truck net.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo boosts E Europe truck net.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it has increased scheduled airfreight road feeder services (RFS) to eastern European destinations.
More feeder services to Cologne to serve freighter flights to Sharjah have also been added.
Hartmut Flessa, Lufthansa Cargo road and rail manager, said the additional capacity had been added flexibly over the last year or under the summer schedules which started on March 30.
Lufthansa had now upgraded the Moscow route to a weekly Boeing 747 freighter flight with ad-hoc RFS departures from a five days a week RFS service, he said.
Warsaw, a fast-growing market, gained a fourth weekly scheduled truck service during the winter 1996-97 timetable, he added.
Scheduled departures had replaced ad-hoc services to Belgrade, Sofia, Kiev, Vilnius, Riga, Tallinn and St Petersburg, Flessa said.

Hans Driedger, general manager capacity management, told Reuters: "Generally most volume for eastern Europe has been from our intercontinental services but in the last few months, tonnage of European origin has increased more and more."
Flessa added that additional truck feeder services were now connecting at Cologne to freighter departures from Lufthansa's Middle East hub at Sharjah.
RFS services between Frankfurt and Stockholm had now been replaced by twice-weekly B747 freighter services under the cargo partnership with SAS Cargo, he added.
